title: The debug service reads the disk, the application only writes to it, and the viewer renders the one thing no existing tool does
scope:
how a developer sees what a request did while it is happening — where a debug record
goes, what carries it to a service, how that service stores and serves it, and what its UI is
allowed to draw. It decides nothing about the probes themselves, which [0018](0018.md) and
[0041](0041.md) own and which this record only consumes, and it does not move `Core\Debug`'s
surface or `Core\Log`'s.
dependsOnText:
[0018](0018.md), whose probe word and named sinks are what produces the stream;
[0092](0092.md), whose record model is what crosses to disk and already answers redaction, elision
and cycles; [0041](0041.md), whose four event kinds and speedscope export are the artifacts this
hands off rather than renders; [0040](0040.md), whose no-bespoke-UI principle this record bounds an
exception to; [0020](0020.md), whose log target is the second thing the service reads.
validatedBy:
the conformance and integration cases the five rules below name, landed by the
goals that carry them. Nothing holds this record on its own today, which is why every rule it
creates is `designed`.

summary.headline: The debug viewer is a separate service that reads files the application wrote
summary.body:
An application writes debug records to a spool file it owns alone and opens no socket for them;
a separate service ingests those files continuously and serves a viewer that only reads. The
viewer renders the one thing no existing tool does, the live stream of correlated requests, and
hands any artifact that already has a good viewer, such as a profile, to that viewer. Writing
the records at all is the `[debug] store` setting, off by default, and it can only reduce what
is kept.
